Resume mi-spectral: SCREEN imputation-engine sensitivity (Bayes-proper DA vs EMB), then
  escalate ONLY if necessary.

  PLAN OF RECORD (read FIRST): todo/017-imputation-engine-sensitivity-screener.md
  It has the full 3-tier DA-minimizing design, decision rules, gotchas, file pointers, and
  first steps. Also skim todo/016's "## GRADING OUTCOME" and the memory note
  [[project-nonmonotone-coxsnell]] for the thread that led here.

  GOAL: decide — as cheaply as possible — whether the paper's PROPER-MI conclusions are
  sensitive to the imputation engine: EMB/Amelia (bootstrap; fast; approximate posterior;
  independent draws) vs Bayes-proper data augmentation (norm::da.norm; conjugate NIW; exact
  stationary law but MCMC/slow). Run DA ONLY if the cheap screener implicates Amelia. If
  conclusions ARE sensitive, add a limitations section to manuscript/derivation.qmd.

  CONTEXT / WHAT'S DONE (todo/015–016, commits 446d1a4, ffff008, 49a2809):
  - Non-monotone (A)+(C): leading-order analytic ≈ −0.22; committed empirical phase-8 rem
    −0.34(n=800)→−0.46(n=1500). GPT-5.5 Layer-3 check found the named extra terms tiny
    (B_cov=−0.02) or cancel (Δ by Louis); live lead = a realized-vs-expected observed-info
    effect under MAR. Reframe is committed and honest.
  - THE WORRY: production proper-MI evidence (W1-amelia, W2, W3, sweeps) rests almost entirely
    on Amelia; da.norm is implemented but barely used; its burnin/thin/rngseed are unvalidated.
  - SCOPE: only the proper-MI WITNESSES are at risk. The Cox–Snell b_Σ and the FIML/analytic
    (A)+(C) are draw-free → robust regardless of how this lands.

  DO THIS SESSION (per todo/017):
  1. Re-read todo/017 + todo/016 GRADING OUTCOME + [[project-nonmonotone-coxsnell]].
  2. STEP 0 (zero new compute): read _modules/w1-information-diagnostic.R outputs (tr_samp
     = Amelia sample RIV vs tr_obs = analytic RIV) and the aggregate H6 verdict (FIML vs
     Amelia within 3pp) in cache/run_all-*/. If Amelia already tracks the analytic, you may
     be done with no new runs.
  3. STEP 1 (Amelia only, NO DA) if inconclusive: paired Amelia-vs-analytic on the stress
     cells (non_monotone MAR, default_Sigma, N∈{200,500}, congenial empri=0, M=200, R≈1000,
     paired seeds). PRIMARY metric = Amelia sample RIV (riv_sample/mi_fit_mvn) vs
     tr_riv_analytic; SECONDARY = W1 T_hat vs ½·tr(RIV), E[A]/tr(RIV). Apply Decision A:
     agree within MCSE → NOT sensitive, document, STOP (do not run DA).
  4. STEP 2 (DA) ONLY if Step 0/1 implicates Amelia: da.norm on the same paired cells,
     rngseed PER WORKER, init EM, provisional burnin=100/thin=50; confirm DA≈analytic but
     Amelia≠analytic → SENSITIVE. If DA also ≠ analytic, suspect DA mixing → validate (§4)
     before concluding.

  CRITICAL GOTCHAS (carried from this thread):
  - em_mvn is UNRELIABLE for the non-monotone design (its rem came out opposite-sign to
    lavaan). Use lavaan FIML or da.norm for fits — NOT em_mvn.
  - Reference everything to the ENGINE-FREE analytic tr(RIV); that's what lets Step 1 conclude
    without DA. Sample-RIV is the low-variance primary metric (rem MCSE grows ≈0.65·√(n/R)).
  - Keep both engines CONGENIAL (Amelia empri=0; da.norm Jeffreys). The sweep's uncongenial
    Amelia (empri=0.5N) is a different axis — don't conflate.
  - Match the estimand: FIML (A)+(C) vs proper-MI (A)+(C) differ (proper ≈ DOUBLES (C) via the
    posterior-draw variance). The engine-free RIV calibration sidesteps this.
  - Use PAIRED data (same simulated dataset per replicate for both engines).
  - da.norm starting values: set θ via norm::makeparam.norm (not Y_mis directly); MLE-start is
    under-dispersed and can HIDE non-convergence — for the §4 R̂ diagnostic use over-dispersed
    starts.

  REPO STATE: on main. R at C:\Program Files\R\R-4.5.1\bin. Engines: impute_mvn (da.norm),
  impute_mvn_amelia in verification/00-setup.R; riv_sample / mi_fit_mvn / tr_riv_analytic /
  fisher_info_obs_mvn vs observed_info_obs_mvn there too. Witnesses: W1-bias-decomposition.R,
  W3-model-selection.R, _modules/{w1-information-diagnostic,w3-sweep,aggregate}.R. If you touch
  the manuscript, `quarto render manuscript/derivation.qmd` must stay exit-0.

  FINISH: record a clear SENSITIVE / NOT-SENSITIVE verdict (+evidence) in todo/017. If NOT
  sensitive: optional one-line engine-robustness note in the derivation. If SENSITIVE: validated-
  DA re-run of the load-bearing cells (over-dispersed multi-start R̂/ESS, rngseed per worker) +
  a limitations section in manuscript/derivation.qmd. Commit on main with the Co-Authored-By
  trailer.
